optional_codes.reason: Furosemide and carvedilol are prescribed drugs taken every day for a chronic condition, which fits category Z79, but no Tabular List instruction requires the code. Defensible either way.

unsupported_codes.reason: Systolic (congestive) heart failure, which includes heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: assigns a type, and the provider states none. The ejection fraction of 30 percent is a test result in the history.
Diastolic (congestive) heart failure: assigns a type the provider does not state.
Combined systolic (congestive) and diastolic (congestive) heart failure: assigns a type the provider does not state.
Left ventricular failure, unspecified: names the left ventricle, which the provider does not state.
Other heart failure, the subcategory for right, biventricular, high output and end stage heart failure: assigns a type the provider does not state.

citations.I50.9: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.B.18: when sufficient clinical information is not known or available about a condition to assign a more specific code, it is acceptable to report the appropriate unspecified code, and it would be inappropriate to select a specific code that is not supported by the medical record documentation. Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. The inclusion terms at I50.9 include 'Cardiac, heart or myocardial failure NOS'. Here the emergency physician's diagnosis is acute on chronic heart failure, with no type; the note records an ejection fraction of 30 percent from an echocardiogram last month, but the physician does not call the heart failure systolic or name a reduced ejection fraction, and category I50 has no code that keeps 'acute on chronic' without a type, so heart failure, unspecified, is reported.

coder_notes: The ejection fraction makes a systolic type clinically likely, but the type has to come from the provider's words. The note states that he has no history of high blood pressure, so no hypertensive heart disease code applies. Shortness of breath, orthopnea and leg swelling are part of the heart failure, and the pulmonary congestion on the film and the natriuretic peptide result are explained by it. He has not missed doses. In practice this documentation would lead to a provider query; the gold is what can be reported from the note as written.
